FOREWORD

8.1 This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 22 June 1984, after the draft finalized by the Spices and Condiments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 Spices and condiments are In common use in this country, Some of them are also exported in considerable quantities. Cardamom is one of the important commodities exported from India. 0.3 This Indian Standard was first published in 1961 and \\ as revised in 1966. This second revision includes requirements for capsules. Changes were made with respect to moisture and volatile oil content based on new data and experience gathered.
0.4 This standard takes into consideration the prevailing methods of trade and has adopted Irades formulated by the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection tor being incorporated in the Agmark ( Grading "nd Mark. ira,) &1'1, framed under the Agrieultural Produc� ( Grading and Alarkin,) Act, 1937.

0.5 In the preparation of this standard, clue consideration has been given to the provisions of the P"lJIntion of Food Adult,ral;on Au, 1954 and the
Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is vubjeet to the Nltrictiona imposed under this Act, wherever applicable. 0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this

.

standard is complied witb, the final value, observed or calculated, expre��io. the result of a test or analysis, shan be rounded off' in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained ia the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value

in this.tandard.
eRul. (or roundinl off numerical values ( "wl,d

).

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements for cardamom, EI,ttIJria

t.11damnlnum (L. )Maton (CHI/OTI ELACHI) of the family Zingiberaceae.

1.2 This standard does not covel' the capsules or
�\mOlllUlll.

~ed~

of the genus

2. REQ,UIREMENTS

2.1 DescriptioD
2.1.1 Cardnmoms witll Capsllus - The cardamoms shall be the nearly rip� fruits of Eleuari� eardamomum ( I.... ) Maton in the COI"m of capsules which have been dried. The capsules shall be of colour ranging from light green to brO\VD, cream and white; global in size or three-cornered having a ribbed appearance. The capsules may he clipped and their pedicels removed. The capsules shall be well formed and wlth sound cardamom seeds inside. The capsules may also be bleached. The cardamoms 111ay be graded on the basis of colour, clipping, size, mass per litre, bleaching or otherwise, proportions of extraneous matter, or place' of origin.
2.1.2 The cardamom seeds capsules may also be decorticated and the separated seeds packed for trade purposes. The cardamom seeds may be graded 011 t he basis of maSI per litre and proportions of extraneous matter ( Sit 2.7) and light seeds ( set 2.11 ).

2.2 Ta.te aDd Aroma or Flayoar - The taste and aroma or flavour of . cardamoms in caspules and seeds shall be characteristic and fresh. The material shall be free from foreign taste and aroma 01" flavour, including rancidity Q.nd mustiness,

2.3 Freedom from Moald_, I���ct_, etc - Cardamoms in capsules
and seeds shall be free from visible moulds and insect infestation.
Nu'd�: - 'rhrip marks alone on call,utes shall not It'Rd to the conclulion that dw capsules have hcrn infested by insects.

2.4 Ma�� per Lltre- The mass of cardamoms in caplules and seed. shall be as prescribed in Table I. The mas of cardamoms contained in one litre shall be determined in accordance wlth the method liven in 4 errs . 1797�1973�.
*Mt'thods of sampJiI1l and test Cor sIlica aDd condimenu.

III 1117 � 1184
'2.5 MoI.t.... e COD teat - The moisture content in all grad. of cardamom except the grade 'Bleached' or 'Half bleached' shall DOt uceed 10 percent ( olm ) when determined in accordance with the methoclliven in 10 of IS : 1797�1973�. The moisture content in the grade Bleached or half bleached shall not exceed 13 percent ( vim) when determined by the same method. -2.6 Volatile 011 Coateat - The volatile oil content of different grades
of cardamom capsules shall be not less than 3�5 percent ( vim) on capsule basis and in the case of seed grades it shall not be less than 4�0 percent ( vIm) on the seed basis when determined in .accordance with the method given in 15 of IS : 1797-1973�.

2.7 Extra.eo�� Matter - The proportion of calyx pieces, stalk bitland other extranec : matter in cardamom in capsules and seeds shall be not more than 5 p .cent and 2 percent by mass, respectively, when determined in accordance with the method given in 5 of IS : 1797-1973�.

2.8 Empty .ad Malformed Cap."le. - The proportion of empty
capsules which are without any seeds or malformed capsules which are scantily filled with seeds shall not be more than 5 percent by count. For this purpose, 100 capsules from the sample shall be opened out and the number of empty and malformed capsules counted.

2.9 I......ture ��d SlIrlvelled Cap.a1e. - The proportion of immature and shrivelled capsules, which are not fully developed, .hall be not
more than 7 percent by mass and shall be determined after separating them in accordance with the method given in 5 of IS : 1797-1973., Percentage of immature and shrivelled capsules shall be not more than the limit prescribed for each grade in Table 1.

2.10 Black���� Spilt. - Blacks include capsules having visible blackish to black colour and spUts include those capsules whioh are op. at corners for more than half the length. The proportion of blacks and splits shall be not more than 15 percent by count. For this purpose, 100 capsules shall be taken from the sample and the number of blacks and splits separated and counted.
2~11 Lillat Seed. - The proportion of light seeds in cardamom seeds shall be not more than 5 percent by mass, when separated in accordance with the method Riven in 5 IS : 1797�1973*. Light seeds shall include seeds which are brown or reel in colour broken or immature and shrivelled.

4. PACKING AND MARKING

4.1.acIdDI
4.1.1 Caplull$ - Cardamoms with capaules shall be packed in clean, sound and dry tinplate containers or wooden casci suitably lined ,vith polyethylene or waterproof paper or kraft paper or in new jute baga lined with polyethylene or waterproof paper. 4.1.2 SeIdl - Cardamom seeds shall be packed in clean and dry tinplate containers or wooden cases lined with polyethylene or waterproof paper or kraft paper.

4.2 Ma~Id., - The following particulars shall be marked on each container:
